subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Should OpenClaw adopt canonical readiness conditions, plugin readiness providers, and standard hosting profiles together as permanent core public contracts?
rationale: The RFC selects new config keys, plugin API, response schema, and readiness-blocking policy; automated review cannot determine whether that breadth is the intended long-term product boundary.

options.title: Accept with compatibility gates
options.body: Approve the combined direction while requiring unset-upgrade, legacy-response, and real conformance proof before acceptance and merge.

options.title: Stage the public surface
options.body: Accept normalized core readiness conditions first and defer plugin providers or operator profiles to a follow-up RFC.

options.title: Decline the core expansion
options.body: Keep profile composition and provider-specific readiness outside a new OpenClaw core contract.

recommendation.title: Accept with compatibility gates
recommendation.body: Approve the combined direction while requiring unset-upgrade, legacy-response, and real conformance proof before acceptance and merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository history most strongly connects this person to the RFC acceptance process and lifecycle contract.
